ground_truth_core_content:
Introduction:
**1:** Both sections cover the Lesson 12/13 recap (Nova research agent, Brown writing workflow, FastMCP/LangGraph framework choices), position system design as the layer above framework selection that determines whether agents feel like polished products or fragile demos, and close with the same decision-framework offering and learning-goals list (thinking tokens, when to parallelize, keeping context lean, human approvals). The generated section compresses three paragraphs into two, but the four underlying design-leverage ideas from the expected section (budgeting reasoning, gating with HITL, controlling context growth, deciding when to parallelize) all have a match in the generated text, the last two appearing via the learning-goals sentence rather than the earlier framing sentence.

A General AI Engineering Decision Framework:
**0:** Six of the seven numbered points cover the same core ideas as the expected section (with different but equivalent illustrative examples, which is acceptable). However, point 2 (Choose Model Family & Capability Mix) is missing three substantive ideas present in the expected section: the startup/hospital named examples for closed-vs-open choice, the entire "match the model's reasoning depth to the task" sub-point (dedicated reasoning models like GPT-5 Thinking/Claude extended thinking/Gemini 2.5 vs faster cheaper models), and the "final consideration is data modality/multimodality" sub-point. Point 5 (Establish a HITL & Evaluation Loop) is also missing the entire evaluation-methodology discussion (small task-specific tests measuring utility/factuality/safety; public leaderboards being a signal but not a substitute for custom evals) and the IT-support-ticket vs stock-trades/press-release autonomy-tier contrast example. These are clear, substantive omissions, not stylistic differences.

Inference-Time Scaling and the Cost/Latency Calculus:
**1:** All four levers (Model Size, Series, Parallel, Input Context Scaling) are covered with matching substance, the Image 1 caption is reproduced verbatim, and the naive-vs-budgeted cost exercise follows the same 5-bullet structure (Model/Input Tokens/Output Tokens/Parallel Runs/Calculation) reaching a comparable ~1000x reduction. The generated section substitutes different models and token counts (Claude 4 Opus/Gemini 2.5 Flash vs the expected section's GPT-5 pro/GPT-5-mini) for the toy calculation, but this is a numeric-example substitution rather than a named-artifact mismatch, since the guideline itself does not mandate specific models for this illustrative exercise.

Our Capstone: Global System Design:
**1:** The Nova and Brown descriptions, the three Brown tools, and the file-based handoff are reproduced with matching substance (in places nearly verbatim), and the generated section adds a well-anchored "stage contract" elaboration. The closing paragraph about article-guideline quality drops the expected section's mechanism explanation ("as we give the LLM more space to interpret, it fills that space with whatever it thinks fits") and its "you don't have to care about how you write, it can be a raw brain dump... delegating to the setup we will teach you" reassurance. Per standing ruling, this is rhetorical/motivational reinforcement of a point the generated section already makes in the same paragraph (vague guidelines produce hollow, gap-filled text) rather than a distinct substantive idea, so it does not count against CoreContent.

Decision Matrix & Defaults for the Capstone:
**1:** Both sections frame the matrix as translating the 7-step framework's abstract principles into a concrete blueprint, describe the row structure (dimension/default/rationale linked to cost, latency, reliability, debuggability), and note the matrix will be referenced repeatedly in later lessons. The generated section's phrasing is if anything closer to the guideline's own wording (e.g. explicitly naming Lessons 15–22) than the expected section's looser paraphrase, but the same underlying ideas are present in both.

Table 1: Decision matrix for the capstone project:
**1:** The table content (all six decision dimensions, default choices, and rationales) is reproduced identically to the expected section.

Conclusion:
**1:** Both sections recap the 7-step framework and its capstone application, make the same "system-level view over single models" argument, note that the decisions/diagrams will be referenced repeatedly in future lessons, and forward-reference the same next-lesson content (Nova's FastMCP server/client, research.md) plus Lessons 19–22 (Brown/LangGraph). The generated section also adds the closing "turning AI engineering from an art into a repeatable engineering practice" line that the guideline requires but the expected section itself omits — an accepted addition, not an omission. The References list differs in length (30 entries vs 9) but serves the same bibliographic purpose.
